knowledgePoint.zh: 词嵌入——语言的分布式表示
knowledgePoint.en: Word embeddings — distributed representations of language

recallIntro.zh: 你闭上眼，思绪飘回了那间深蓝色的教室。今天的大屏幕上显示着一个三维坐标空间，里面散布着许多发光的小点，每个点旁边标注着一个词。本吉奥教授站在屏幕前，手指在空中比画着那些点之间看不见的连线，眼中闪烁着哲学家面对深刻真理时的光芒。
recallIntro.en: You close your eyes, and your thoughts drift back to that deep blue classroom. Today the large screen shows a three-dimensional coordinate space scattered with glowing dots, each labeled with a word. Prof. Bengio stands before the screen, tracing invisible lines between the dots with his finger, his eyes shining with the light of a philosopher confronting a profound truth.

recallOutro.zh: 你回过神来，词嵌入的核心思想仍在脑海中回荡。每个词都是高维空间中的一个点，词与词之间的距离和方向编码了它们的语义关系。「国王减去男人加上女人等于女王」，这个简单的等式背后是一个深刻的发现：语言中的意义可以被几何化。
recallOutro.en: You return to the present. The core idea of word embeddings still echoes in your mind — every word is a point in high-dimensional space, and the distances and directions between words encode their semantic relationships. 「King minus man plus woman equals queen」 — behind this simple equation lies a profound discovery: meaning in language can be geometrized.

text.zh: 教室的大屏幕上显示着一个奇怪的画面：成千上万个小点悬浮在黑色的三维空间中，每个点旁边有一个极小的标签。本吉奥教授走进来，手里拿着一个遥控器。他按了一下按钮，视角旋转了。你看到那些看似随机的点其实形成了清晰的簇，动物的词聚在一起，颜色的词聚在一起，国家的词也聚在一起。
text.en: The classroom's large screen shows a curious image — thousands of tiny dots suspended in a black three-dimensional space, each with a minuscule label beside it. Prof. Bengio walks in holding a remote. He presses a button, the viewpoint rotates, and you see that the seemingly random dots actually form clear clusters — animal words cluster together, color words cluster together, country words cluster together.

text.zh: 你们看到屏幕上的这些点了吗？每一个点代表一个英语单词。它们在空间中的位置不是随机的——意思相近的词会靠在一起，意思不同的词会分开。今天我要告诉你们这些点是怎么来的，以及它们为什么让我如此兴奋。
text.en: See these dots on the screen? Each dot represents an English word. Their positions in space aren't random — words with similar meanings cluster together, and words with different meanings separate. Today I'll tell you where these dots come from, and why they excite me so much.

text.zh: 先来看看传统的做法。如果你的词汇表有10000个词，最简单的方式是给每个词分配一个编号——「猫」是第342号，「狗」是第1057号。在数学上，我们用一个10000维的向量来表示每个词，其中只有一个位置是1，其余都是0。这叫做「独热编码」。
text.en: Let's first look at the traditional approach. If your vocabulary has 10,000 words, the simplest method is to assign each word a number — 「cat」 is number 342, 「dog」 is number 1057. Mathematically, we represent each word as a 10,000-dimensional vector with only one position being 1 and all others 0. This is called 「one-hot encoding」.

text.zh: 独热编码有一个根本性的缺陷：在它眼里，任何两个词之间的距离都是一样的。「猫」和「狗」的距离等于「猫」和「经济学」的距离。但我们知道「猫」和「狗」应该更近，因为它们都是动物、都是宠物。独热编码完全丢失了这种语义上的亲疏关系。
text.en: One-hot encoding has a fundamental flaw — in its eyes, the distance between any two words is the same. The distance between 「cat」 and 「dog」 equals the distance between 「cat」 and 「economics」. But we know 「cat」 and 「dog」 should be closer — they're both animals, both pets. One-hot encoding completely loses this semantic kinship.

text.zh: 如果要让词的表示能够反映语义关系，你觉得关键的改变是什么？
text.en: If word representations need to reflect semantic relationships, what do you think is the key change needed?

text.zh: 用更少的维度、更密集的数字来表示每个词，让每个维度都有意义
text.en: Use fewer dimensions with denser numbers to represent each word, making every dimension meaningful

text.zh: 非常好。这正是核心思路。把一个10000维的稀疏向量（只有一个1）压缩成一个几百维的密集向量（每个维度都是有意义的实数），这种表示被称为{词嵌入}。「嵌入」的意思就是把离散的符号嵌入到一个连续的向量空间中。在这个空间里，距离和方向都有语义含义。
text.en: Excellent. That's precisely the core idea. Compressing a 10,000-dimensional sparse vector (with just one 1) into a dense vector of a few hundred dimensions (where every dimension is a meaningful real number) — this representation is called a {word embedding}. 「Embedding」 means embedding discrete symbols into a continuous vector space. In this space, distances and directions carry semantic meaning.

text.zh: 从词的上下文来学习它的表示——经常出现在相似语境中的词应该有相似的表示
text.en: Learn a word's representation from its context — words that frequently appear in similar contexts should have similar representations

text.zh: 你说到了一个非常重要的语言学原理——分布假说：一个词的意义由它出现的语境决定。「猫」和「狗」经常出现在相似的语境中（「我养了一只__」「__在沙发上睡觉」），所以它们的表示应该相近。这个直觉正是{词嵌入}训练的基础。我们通过大量文本让网络学习每个词的向量表示。
text.en: You've touched on a very important linguistic principle — the distributional hypothesis: a word's meaning is determined by the contexts in which it appears. 「Cat」 and 「dog」 often appear in similar contexts (「I have a __」, 「__ is sleeping on the couch」), so their representations should be close. This intuition is exactly the foundation for training {word embeddings}. We train networks on large amounts of text to learn each word's vector representation.

text.zh: 让语言学家手动标注词之间的关系，然后把这些关系编码到表示中
text.en: Have linguists manually annotate relationships between words, then encode those relationships into the representations

text.zh: 这是一个合理的直觉。实际上，早期的自然语言处理确实依赖于手工构建的词典和语义网络，比如WordNet。但人工标注的规模有限，很难覆盖词义的全部细微差别。更让人兴奋的是，我们发现可以让网络从大量原始文本中自动学习{词嵌入}，完全不需要任何人工标注，效果反而更好。
text.en: That's a reasonable intuition — in fact, early NLP did rely on hand-built dictionaries and semantic networks like WordNet. But manual annotation has limited scale and can hardly cover all the nuances of word meaning. What's more exciting is that we've discovered networks can learn {word embeddings} automatically from large amounts of raw text — without any human annotation, and the results are actually better.

text.zh: 2003年，我和同事发表了一篇关于神经网络语言模型的论文。我们的想法很简单：训练一个网络来预测下一个词。给它「猫坐在」，让它猜下一个词可能是什么。「垫子上」的概率很高，「飞机」的概率则很低。为了完成这个任务，网络必须学会把每个词映射到一个{分布式表示}，也就是一个稠密的向量。
text.en: In 2003, my colleagues and I published a paper on neural network language models. Our idea was simple: train a network to predict the next word. Give it 「the cat sat on the」 and have it guess what comes next — 「mat」 has high probability, 「airplane」 has low probability. To accomplish this task, the network must learn to map each word to a {distributed representation} — a dense vector.

text.zh: 十年之后，2013年，谷歌的米科洛夫把这个思路推向了一个新的高度。他提出了{Word2Vec}——一种更高效的词嵌入训练方法。Word2Vec可以在几个小时内处理数十亿词的语料，生成高质量的词向量。它的速度和效果都让人惊叹。
text.en: Ten years later, in 2013, Google's Mikolov took this idea to a new level. He proposed {Word2Vec} — a more efficient method for training word embeddings. Word2Vec can process billions of words in just a few hours, producing high-quality word vectors. Both its speed and results are astonishing.

text.zh: 但最让人震撼的是Word2Vec揭示的词向量的几何性质。看这个——如果你取「国王」的向量，减去「男人」的向量，再加上「女人」的向量，你得到的结果最接近「女王」的向量。「国王」减去「男人」加上「女人」等于「女王」。
text.en: But the most stunning thing is the geometric properties that Word2Vec reveals in word vectors. Look at this — if you take the vector for 「king」, subtract the vector for 「man」, and add the vector for 「woman」, the result is closest to the vector for 「queen」. King minus man plus woman equals queen.

text.zh: 本吉奥教授按下遥控器，屏幕上的三维空间旋转了一下。四个发光的点被高亮显示——「king」「queen」「man」「woman」。它们之间画出了两条平行的箭头，一条从「man」指向「woman」，另一条从「king」指向「queen」。两条箭头的方向和长度几乎一模一样。
text.en: Prof. Bengio presses the remote and the three-dimensional space on screen rotates. Four glowing dots are highlighted — 「king」, 「queen」, 「man」, 「woman」. Two parallel arrows are drawn between them — one from 「man」 to 「woman」, another from 「king」 to 「queen」. The direction and length of both arrows are nearly identical.

text.zh: 这意味着什么？这意味着网络仅通过预测下一个词的任务，就能从纯文本中自动学会「性别」这样的抽象概念，并把它编码为向量空间中的一个方向。同样，「巴黎减去法国加上日本」的结果会接近「东京」，这表明「首都」这样的关系也被编码为一个方向。于是，语言中的意义就变成了可计算的几何关系。
text.en: What does this mean? It means the network, from pure text alone, just by predicting the next word, automatically learned the abstract concept of 「gender」 — and encoded it as a direction in vector space. Similarly, 「Paris minus France plus Japan」 approximates 「Tokyo」 — the 「capital」 relationship is also encoded as a direction. Meaning in language becomes computable geometric relationships.

text.zh: 词向量能够捕捉语义类比关系（国王:女王 = 男人:女人）。你觉得这说明了什么关于语言和意义的深层问题？
text.en: Word vectors can capture semantic analogies (king:queen = man:woman). What do you think this reveals about deeper questions of language and meaning?

text.zh: 语言的意义有内在的数学结构——词义之间的关系可以用向量运算来表达
text.en: The meaning of language has an inherent mathematical structure — relationships between word meanings can be expressed through vector operations

text.zh: 这是一个让我夜不能寐的想法。如果意义真的有数学结构，那「理解」这件事也许可以被形式化。当然，词向量捕捉的只是统计上的共现模式——它知道「国王」和「女王」的关系类似于「男人」和「女人」的关系，但它未必真的「理解」什么是性别。不过，统计模式和真正的理解之间的边界在哪里呢？这是一个我们仍在探索的问题。
text.en: This is an idea that keeps me up at night. If meaning truly has mathematical structure, then 「understanding」 might be formalizable. Of course, word vectors only capture statistical co-occurrence patterns — the network knows the relationship between 「king」 and 「queen」 is similar to 「man」 and 「woman」, but it may not truly 「understand」 what gender is. However, where is the boundary between statistical patterns and true understanding? That's a question we're still exploring.

text.zh: 也许词的意义真的可以完全由它的使用方式决定——「用法即意义」
text.en: Maybe a word's meaning really can be entirely determined by how it's used — 「usage is meaning」

text.zh: 你在引用维特根斯坦的语言哲学——「一个词的意义就是它在语言中的用法」。词嵌入的成功似乎在某种程度上验证了这个哲学观点。如果一个系统从来没有见过真实的猫，但它读过所有包含「猫」这个词的句子，它学到的「猫」的表示包含了多少关于猫的真实知识？这个问题的答案可能比我们想象的更复杂。
text.en: You're referencing Wittgenstein's philosophy of language — 「the meaning of a word is its use in the language」. The success of word embeddings seems to validate this philosophical view to some extent. If a system has never seen a real cat but has read every sentence containing the word 「cat」, how much real knowledge about cats does its learned representation of 「cat」 contain? The answer may be more complex than we imagine.

text.zh: 这些只是统计相关性——网络并没有真正理解词义，只是学会了词的共现模式
text.en: These are just statistical correlations — the network doesn't truly understand word meaning, it has only learned co-occurrence patterns

text.zh: 这是一个非常值得认真对待的批评。词向量确实是从统计共现中学到的——它反映的是词在文本中的分布规律，而非对世界的直接感知。「国王减男人加女人等于女王」可能只是因为这四个词在训练语料中有特定的共现模式。但我想反问一个问题：人类学习词义的过程，在多大程度上也依赖于语境中的统计规律？也许差距没有我们以为的那么大。
text.en: This is a criticism that deserves serious consideration. Word vectors are indeed learned from statistical co-occurrence — they reflect how words distribute in text, not direct perception of the world. 「King minus man plus woman equals queen」 may just be because these four words have specific co-occurrence patterns in training data. But let me ask in return: to what extent does human word learning also depend on statistical patterns in context? Perhaps the gap is smaller than we think.

text.zh: 不管怎样，词嵌入已经在实践中证明了它的价值。它解决了一个困扰自然语言处理多年的问题——如何让机器以连续、稠密、有意义的方式表示词语。有了词嵌入，我们终于可以把人类语言真正「输入」到神经网络中了。
text.en: Regardless, word embeddings have proven their value in practice. They solved a problem that plagued natural language processing for years — how to let machines represent words in a continuous, dense, meaningful way. With word embeddings, we can finally truly 「input」 human language into neural networks.

suggestedContent.zh: 词嵌入将离散的词语映射为连续向量空间中的点，语义相近的词距离更近。Word2Vec（2013年）揭示了向量的几何性质：「国王-男人+女人≈女王」。词嵌入通过预测语境中的词来学习，无需人工标注。核心哲学问题：统计模式与真正的语义理解之间的边界在哪里？
suggestedContent.en: Word embeddings map discrete words to points in continuous vector space, where semantically similar words are closer. Word2Vec (2013) revealed geometric properties of vectors: 「king - man + woman ≈ queen」. Embeddings are learned by predicting words in context, requiring no manual annotation. Core philosophical question: where is the boundary between statistical patterns and true semantic understanding?

text.zh: 现在我们有了两个关键的工具。LSTM让我们能处理序列，词嵌入让我们能表示语言。接下来的问题是：我们能不能把它们组合起来，解决一个真正困难的问题？比如——机器翻译。把一种语言的句子变成另一种语言的句子。下节课，我会介绍一个优美的架构：编码器-解码器。
text.en: Now we have two key tools. LSTM lets us process sequences, and word embeddings let us represent language. The next question is: can we combine them to solve a truly difficult problem? For example — machine translation. Turning a sentence in one language into a sentence in another. Next lesson, I'll introduce an elegant architecture: the encoder-decoder.

text.zh: 今天我想让你们记住一件事：当我们把词变成向量空间中的点时，我们做了一件非常深刻的事情——我们把人类语言中最离散、最符号化的部分，变成了连续的、可微的数学对象。这意味着我们可以对意义做微积分。这个想法的力量，也许我们现在还远远没有完全意识到。
text.en: I want you to remember one thing today: when we turn words into points in vector space, we've done something very profound — we've transformed the most discrete, most symbolic part of human language into continuous, differentiable mathematical objects. This means we can do calculus on meaning. The power of this idea — perhaps we haven't yet come close to fully realizing it.

text.zh: 本吉奥教授按下遥控器，屏幕上的三维词向量空间缓缓旋转。那些发光的点像星星一样悬浮在深蓝色的虚空中。他看着屏幕，轻声说：「每一个词都是一颗星星。我们正在学习阅读这片星空的语法。」他拿起笔记本，安静地走出了教室。屏幕上的星空继续旋转着，语言的几何在黑暗中闪烁。
text.en: Prof. Bengio presses the remote, and the three-dimensional word vector space on screen slowly rotates. The glowing dots float like stars in the deep blue void. He watches the screen and says softly: 「Every word is a star. We are learning to read the grammar of this sky」. He picks up his notebook and walks quietly out of the classroom. The star field on screen continues to rotate, the geometry of language glimmering in the darkness.
